title: Research Evidence Observatory
subtitle: An inspectable bridge from experiments to evidence-based research.

cases.label: Evidence explorer
cases.title: Ask a question. Follow the evidence.
cases.description: Search actual experiment records across four public research projects. Every result carries its source URL, content digest, measured metrics and limitations. No model or API is called by this offline explorer.
method: A portable JSON registry snapshots public study artifacts. Each record contains source repository, experiment ID, source-artifact SHA-256, content SHA-256, typed metrics, methods and limitations.
BM25 term weighting (k₁=1.2, b=0.75) ranks original experiment records. Ties use source ID. Empty lexical support causes abstention; scores are relevance weights, not confidence probabilities.
The browser performs deterministic retrieval locally. Python provides an extractive answer interface and a bounded JSON evidence export for research workflows.
limitations: Thirteen authored regression questions are small development fixtures, not an independent held-out benchmark. Failed queries remain in the table.

The guaranteed-profit question deliberately shares corpus terms but has no supporting answer: BM25 retrieves anyway. Empty-lexical-support abstention does not detect semantic false support. No semantic answer correctness or hallucination rate is estimated.

Snapshots can become stale. Source artifact digests identify exactly which local public report was ingested; re-ingestion is explicit. Registry hashes detect accidental edits, not a malicious party able to rewrite both data and hashes.

cases.label: Claim audit & integration
cases.title: Check the number before it becomes a claim.
cases.description: A numeric claim must name an existing experiment, a recorded metric, its exact unit and a matching value. Export source-labelled context for evidence-based analysis.
method: Claim validation uses exact source IDs and metric labels, exact unit strings and numeric isclose tolerance 10⁻⁶ relative / 10⁻⁸ absolute. It never changes units implicitly.

Source text is serialized as JSON evidence under a data-only header. Context export is capped at 8,000 characters by default and accepts a bounded 500–32,000-character setting. Complete records are included; records are not silently truncated.
The adapter exports bounded, source-labelled evidence for research analysis. It does not invoke an external model provider.
limitations: Matching a recorded number verifies transcription only. It does not validate the underlying study or establish causality, profitability or quantum advantage.
Five specified claim probes demonstrate interface behavior, not robustness to all adversarial inputs. JSON boundaries and instructions do not guarantee an LLM will resist prompt injection.
The browser and CLI use deterministic retrieval and do not generate prose using an LLM.

method: Freeze manifest fingerprints all ten records, the Python retriever and browser implementation before question authoring. Evaluation fails on drift; settings and questions were not tuned on confirmation outcomes.

Twenty answerable questions cover every record twice; four unrelated unanswerables and six misleading lexical overlaps have no supporting source. Labels and rationales were fixed before running either method.
Baseline counts unique matching terms using the same fields, tokenizer, positive-score filter and source-ID ties. Both methods are evaluated at ranks 1 and 3; no cutoff is selected from outcomes.

Source recall uses only answerable questions. False support is any nonempty retrieval on an unanswerable question, a retrieval-as-support risk proxy. Empty retrieval is counted separately by answerability and stratum in results/AI01-confirmation.json.
Freeze SHA-256: d4f79ac5bec62dfba720a5d7d8ac2d77a7e995357ee849fdea5f9bf491ce2261; question SHA-256: f9d2e6e5246cdba01ad2cbcb7a5a7effbc2c420a23ac53933f6ef70116ef7d2c
limitations: These are authored, source-aware confirmation questions, independent of parameter selection but not blinded or representative user samples. No population accuracy or statistical superiority is established.
Returning related evidence does not assert entailment. False support measures the risk of treating retrieval as an answer, not an LLM hallucination rate; no LLM is used.
Source recall does not grade extracted answers. Shared methods across near-duplicate records can confuse rank 1. Hashes expose accidental drift but are not tamper-proof provenance.

rows: Units, dataset, evaluation protocol and quantity match
Units, dataset, evaluation protocol and quantity match
Unit mismatch: exact strings required; no implicit conversion
Quantity mismatch: 99% value at risk versus 99% expected shortfall
Exactly one reviewed comparison contract is required for each metric

method: Select two registered numeric metrics below. Values come from the registry; callers cannot substitute claimed numbers. Accepted differences are left minus right.

Exact unit, dataset, evaluation protocol and quantity identities must match. Dataset IDs are case-specific; a common project, seed or source artifact is insufficient. Nominal targets and empirical coverage use different protocols.

Reviewed contracts in docs/comparison-contracts.json bind values, units and source fingerprints. Missing metadata, ambiguous IDs, non-finite values and stale contracts fail closed. Empty units need reviewed quantity identities.
The unit-only baseline checks exact unit strings and therefore admits cross-regime MAE, nominal versus empirical coverage, different USD quantities and unrelated unreviewed counts.

limitations: Authored contract probes, not population accuracy. Curated identities are review assertions over a saved synthetic artifact, not independently verified raw-data hashes.
Differences describe saved point estimates only; no uncertainty, significance, causal effect or real-market performance is inferred.
An empty source unit remains empty; quantity IDs disambiguate it without inventing physical units. Unreviewed metrics are rejected.

cases.label: Registry freshness audit
cases.title: Detect source drift. Keep the previous evidence.
cases.description: Can artifact-byte checks detect changes missed by indexed-text checks while preserving reproducible prior evidence?
method: Synthetic source envelopes project all ten saved registry records with their metrics and full text; mutations are controlled fault injections, not observations of live source changes.

Refresh hashes the exact bytes read once for each allowlisted source. It reports unchanged, stale, missing, invalid or unverifiable states with old/new digests and case IDs. Indexed-text hashes form the baseline.

Before replacement, content-addressed history retains the exact prior registry, observed raw sources, candidate registry and audit. Existing history files cannot be overwritten with different bytes; invalid sources block publication. Stable source IDs remain stable; removed IDs remain in prior snapshots.

Inspect controlled scenarios below, or use the offline refresh command with explicit source files. A source unavailable locally is unknown, never certified fresh. Public registry SHA-256: f9cae56d0b0258a8d2faf57190e731e1c4bbc83bac72aea22a21f4afaa538fe6
limitations: Controlled synthetic fault injections, not a live freshness survey or an accuracy estimate. No network refresh or companion experiment was run.

Byte changes include formatting and source metadata: stale means different bytes, not necessarily different scientific results. Unavailable or invalid sources have unknown freshness and block replacement.

Prior registry snapshots retain complete recorded IDs, metrics and evidence text. Original raw sources absent from history cannot be reconstructed; this is reported explicitly. Stored hashes do not authenticate an adversary rewriting both bytes and hashes.
A refreshed registry needs new retrieval protocols and reviewed comparison contracts. Existing frozen inputs are preserved; no compute-cost advantage or model inference is measured.

method: Before new questions were authored, freeze manifest fixed full registry bytes, Python/browser retrievers, baseline, evaluator, earlier questions, cutoffs and question counts. The complete new set was then sealed before evaluation. Drift fails closed.

Two answerable questions per source, four unrelated unsupported topics and four absent measurements with overlapping vocabulary. Exact answerable source anchors are validated against frozen evidence text. No rules, questions or labels were changed after evaluation.
Baseline uses unique-term intersection on the same title/text, tokenizer, positive-score filter and source-ID tie break as BM25. Both use ranks 1 and 3.
At each cutoff, answerable hits plus wrong-source misses plus empty misses equal 20. Unsupported false support plus empty retrieval equal 8; unsupported questions never inflate source recall.

limitations: Source-aware authored questions with earlier results visible; not blind authorship, user sampling or population accuracy. Source anchors check label traceability, not semantic correctness automatically.
Any unsupported retrieval is a risk proxy: a limitation that rejects a premise is useful evidence but does not supply the absent measurement. No LLM or answer-generation quality is evaluated.

Saved records describe small synthetic experiments. Hashes identify drift, not authenticity or external timestamps. No runtime or cost advantage is measured; no significance claim follows from these counts.

provenance: Registry derived solely from the four public companion study artifacts. No unpublished research, credentials or paper text is ingested.
